title: Lemon Drizzle Loaf
subtitle: Zingy lemon sponge with a crunchy honey drizzle
excerpt: A reliably moist loaf with a proper crust from the hot drizzle poured on straight out of the oven. The crumb stays tender for days. One bowl, no mixer needed.
sourceNotes: Lemon drizzle cake became a British baking favourite in the 1970s and has been a fixture of home baking ever since. The drizzle technique of pouring syrup over a hot cake to form a crust was popularised by Evelyn Rose.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before adding the drizzle. Wrap tightly and freeze for up to 3 months. Drizzle after thawing.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps wrapped at room temperature for 4 days. The crust softens a little after day one but the flavour improves.

content.text: Pour the drizzle over the loaf while it is still hot and in the tin. This is what creates the crunchy crust rather than a sticky glaze.

items.prepNote: zest for the loaf, juice for the drizzle

content.text: Heat the oven to 180C. Grease a 900g loaf tin and line with baking paper.
Beat the butter and honey together until pale and fluffy.
Add the eggs one at a time. Beat well after each addition.
Add the lemon zest. Fold in the flour until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour into the tin. Smooth the top.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes. A skewer inserted in the centre should come out clean.
While the loaf bakes, squeeze the lemon juice into a small bowl.
As soon as the loaf comes out of the oven, pour the juice all over the top while still in the tin.
Leave to cool fully in the tin before slicing.

items.cause: Underbaked or oven door opened too early.
items.fix: Test with a skewer. Do not open the oven before 35 minutes.

items.cause: Loaf had cooled before the juice was added.
items.fix: Drizzle immediately once the tin leaves the oven.
Weigh flour carefully. Check oven at 40 minutes.
